missions.text: Three passes first: every goal needs 3 passes before the shot.
Left foot day: only left-foot goals count.
Everyone touches: every teammate touches the ball before a goal.
Slow motion: walk speed for 1 minute.
Youngest first: the youngest player takes the first pass.
Cone shot: shoot from behind the cone for double points.
Name a club: before a kick, say a UAE club (Al Ain, Al Wahda, Al Jazira).
Goalie swap: the goalkeeper changes after each goal.
Golden minute: goals in the last minute count double.
Yalla chant: the scoring team shouts “Yalla!” together.

riddles.question: I pour hospitality in tiny cups and have a long spout.
I am sweet, I grow on a palm and I go with coffee.
I fly high, wear a little hood and live with my Emirati friend.
I have no legs but I cross the sea with a big sail.
I hide in a shell under the sea and become a treasure.
I am the ship of the desert and I walk far in the sand.
I am a small wooden boat that carries people across the Creek.
I am the room where family and guests sit, talk and drink coffee.

tales: The old nakhuda smiles: a pearl in the net!
A tiny pearl glimmers in the blue.
A calm tide reveals a little treasure.
A shiny pearl catches the sun.
The diver finds a bright treasure in the sand.
A silver shimmer rises from the sea.
A golden pearl glows in the shell.
A rare treasure makes the crew cheer.
The sea gives up a golden prize.
A treasure chest rests beneath the dhow.
The crew discovers a chest of pearls.
A hidden chest brings a great haul.
Oh no, a jellyfish drifts by. Pile gone!

The diver spots a jellyfish and returns to shore.

choices: Stand, say “Hayyak Allah” and offer a seat
manners.reason: Welcoming guests warmly is a big part of Emirati hospitality.

manners.scenario: You have had enough Arabic coffee.
choices: Gently shake the small cup and hand it back
manners.reason: Gently shaking the cup is a polite signal that you have had enough.

choices: Take with your right hand and say thank you
manners.reason: Accepting with the right hand and thanking your host shows respect.
Standing to greet an elder is a thoughtful sign of respect.

choices: Wait for the elder or host to start
manners.reason: Waiting for the host or elder is considerate at a shared meal.

choices: Walk them to the door and say “Fi amanillah”
manners.reason: A warm farewell helps guests feel welcome until they leave.
